openingMemo: Miami is where I want to start Sunday. San Francisco and Buffalo are next. Green Bay has the biggest gap on the sheet, but its offensive line needs an answer before Thursday. Chicago’s quarterback keeps me from taking its number very far.
I have six games worth a closer look below. No order on this opening copy.
scheduleMemo: Thursday: Atlanta at Green Bay. Sunday has nine games at 10:00, two at 13:05, two at 13:25 and the Rams at Denver at 17:20. Philadelphia at Chicago finishes the week Monday. All times Pacific.
changeMemo: This is the Week 3 opening sheet. The September 8 Week 1 edition stays in the archive; those old prices are closed.

The September 22 Graham board includes the latest Atlanta and Indianapolis replacement estimates. Indianapolis has cleared its unresolved warning. Green Bay’s line, Detroit’s secondary and the Giants, Seattle and Chicago quarterbacks remain open questions.
Pinnacle comparison: September 22, 18:09 Pacific. The market column is a dated reference.

reviews.read: Green Bay gets my attention first because it plays Thursday. Twelve from Graham against five and a half on the board is a serious disagreement. I don’t trust the full gap while the Packers’ line situation is unresolved. Atlanta’s Terrell adjustment is included, with Henderson treated as the replacement estimate. The market has moved a point toward Atlanta in the saved comparison. I want the protection question settled before going further with Green Bay.
reviews.note: Packers line first. The six-and-a-half-point gap can wait.

reviews.read: Buffalo is one of the first Sunday games I want back. Graham makes the Bills eleven; the board has seven and a half. I like the direction, although laying the hook above seven gives me less room than a glance at the gap suggests. No unresolved personnel or quarterback flag on this number. It earns a proper look at the price.
Cleveland gets a half-point more than Graham allows, with the board giving them three. That is worth noticing at three, but it is a small disagreement and I have stronger questions elsewhere.

A point toward Detroit isn’t enough to hold my interest while the secondary is unsettled. Graham has eight against seven, but I want to know who is taking those replacement duties before spending more time here.

Indianapolis is more interesting now. Graham still has the Colts favored by a half after the personnel estimates; the board gives them three. The Pierce estimate assumes Treadwell and Slayton split the added receiver work equally. That split is an assumption, and I’ll revisit this if one takes most of the role. For now, Indianapolis belongs on my short list.
reviews.note: Colts worth another look. Watch the receiver split.

reviews.read: I want another look at New England getting three. Graham has the game even, and there is no unresolved personnel or quarterback flag on his number. The full field goal is the attraction. The saved market comparison is unchanged, so movement adds nothing to the case.
reviews.note: Patriots stay on the short list.

reviews.read: Miami is my first Sunday review. I have no quarrel with Kansas City being favored. Eleven and a half is a different argument when Graham has five and a half. Six points is a big enough disagreement that I want to challenge our number as carefully as the market’s. No unresolved personnel or quarterback flag here. If the assessment holds up, this is the dog I want to spend time on.
I’m leaving this alone until the Giants’ quarterback is confirmed. Four from Graham against three on the board gives New York a point, and that is too little to carry an unsettled starter.

Pittsburgh interests me more than the size of the gap might suggest. Graham asks Cincinnati to lay two; the board asks three and a half. Getting the Steelers beyond three is the part I care about. This sits behind the larger Sunday disagreements, but it stays on my list.
reviews.note: Steelers: the half above three matters.

reviews.read: Washington is the side the comparison points to: seven against Graham’s five and a half. Seattle’s starter is still unresolved in this review, so I’m putting this aside until that changes. I don’t have enough conviction in the gap yet.
reviews.note: Seattle starter needed before another read.

reviews.read: San Francisco is my first afternoon review. Graham has fourteen against eight and a half, a five-and-a-half-point difference with no unresolved personnel or quarterback flag. That is substantial, but I would still be asking a favorite to cover more than a touchdown. I want a firm reason to trust the fourteen before I get comfortable laying eight and a half.
Tampa Bay gets two against Graham’s one and a half. Nothing much for me here; that half-point leaves this well down the afternoon list.

New Orleans at three and a half is a point shorter than Graham’s four and a half. The direction is toward the Saints, but I’m still laying more than three for a modest difference. I prefer the other afternoon work.

Baltimore three against Graham’s three and a half deserves a small mark. I would rather lay three than three and a half, certainly, but a half-point on its own doesn’t move this near the top of my week.
reviews.note: Ravens: price matters on a small difference.

reviews.read: Denver getting two and a half interests me a little. Graham makes the Rams one, so there is a point and a half toward the home dog. I would rather work through Miami, Indianapolis and New England first. Denver stays as a secondary Sunday-night review.
reviews.note: Broncos behind the main Sunday list.

reviews.read: Chicago is the number I’m least willing to take at face value. Graham has the Bears favored by one; the board has Philadelphia favored by four and a half. That is five and a half points apart, but Chicago’s starter is still unconfirmed. The market has moved another point toward Philadelphia in the saved comparison. I want the quarterback answer before I decide how much of this disagreement deserves my attention.
reviews.note: Do not rank Chicago on the gap alone.

closingWatchlist: 1. MIAMI — First Sunday review. Six points between Graham and the board, with no unresolved input flag. I want to understand that disagreement before trusting it.
2. SAN FRANCISCO — First afternoon review. Five and a half points apart; the question is whether fourteen is a fair demand of the favorite.
3. BUFFALO — Three and a half points toward the Bills. The seven-and-a-half-point spread makes the price important.
4. INDIANAPOLIS — The Colts are favored on Graham’s sheet and getting three on the board. Keep the receiver-role estimate under review.
5. NEW ENGLAND — Three points in a game Graham makes even. A straightforward reason to look again.
6. PITTSBURGH — Smaller gap, but getting three and a half against a fair of two deserves attention.

Before Thursday, settle Green Bay’s line. Chicago stays outside that ranking until the quarterback is confirmed. Detroit, the Giants and Seattle–Washington also need their outstanding answers. Denver is my next secondary review.
signature: That is where I’m spending my time this week. — Bill
currentMood: Reserved and direct. Miami, San Francisco and Buffalo lead the Week 3 review priorities; Indianapolis, New England and Pittsburgh complete the short list. Green Bay needs its line resolved before Thursday; Chicago needs a confirmed quarterback. No order.
